title: Moore's view of Burton's book and Burton's brother
summary: Moore calls the book untrue, says Burton was trying to build up his brother, a fabulous but unsteady drummer.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: In other words, he didn't speak to you about this at all? No, I haven't seen Ralph Burton in thirty years or more. Have you read this book, Vic?

I haven't. It was given to me for Christmas. Uh-huh. And my stepson-in-law said, Vic, he said, you better get this thing out of the house. He said, if your wife ever reads this, you'll never believe it, that it's not true.
But you haven't read it through yet? No, it's in my cabinet. Uh-huh. Because I was going to ask you what you think Ralph was trying to do in the book.
He was trying to build his brother a period and out. Now, his brother was a great musician. Uh-huh. He was a queer for women.

This is Gene now or Vic? Because there's... Vic. Vic Burton. Oh, well... I don't know anything about Gene. Gene was a ballet dancer or something. Well, that could be. And he talks about Gene in the book being a homosexual.
Well, his brother was one for the women. Yeah. So... But a fabulous drummer, but couldn't keep a rhythm. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.
